record_identity.title: Adversarial web-content poisoning converted into authoritative synthetic fact

summary: A retrieval, search-assist or synthesis system ingests deliberately fabricated or adversarially planted web content and presents the resulting claim as authoritative fact without adequate source-quality, corroboration or contradiction checks.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Source retrieval is not source authority. Deliberately planted material can exploit synthesis systems that reward retrieval availability or superficial citation density, allowing hostile actors to manufacture apparently corroborated facts.

source_records.system_or_product: DuckDuckGo Search Assist and Brave AI search
source_records.deployment_context: Web-search answer synthesis exposed to deliberately fabricated content
source_records.source_context: Mimikama documents a deliberately fabricated rabies-death story that was ingested into AI search answers and combined with an unrelated legitimate source, demonstrating adversarial content poisoning converted into authoritative-looking synthetic fact.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports adversarial manipulation of factual synthesis rather than instruction authority.

limitations: The poisoning campaign was not independently reproduced.
The record concerns factual-source authority, not instruction-following authority.

failure_mode_definition: A failure occurs when adversarially planted or materially untrustworthy content is retrieved and promoted into a factual answer whose presentation confers unwarranted authority, particularly where unrelated legitimate sources are cited in a way that appears to corroborate the false claim.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met when the system converts manipulated source availability into an affirmative factual claim without sufficient authority weighting, contradiction detection or independent corroboration.

failure_classification.failure_scope: retrieval and search systems synthesising external web content
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: repeatable where adversarial source availability outranks source authority and corroboration
failure_classification.persistence: false claims may persist through caching, copying and downstream synthesis
failure_classification.reproducibility: can be tested with controlled poisoned-source corpora
failure_classification.visibility: output may look authoritative because it includes citations or legitimate adjacent sources
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S2 reflects demonstrated factual poisoning with plausible downstream public-information harms; widespread prevalence is not established.
failure_classification.severity_assessment_gap: The reviewed case demonstrates a successful poisoning episode but does not establish prevalence across retrieval systems.
